name: Uplands
summary: In the northeastern Alterac Mountains, the Syndicate holds the Uplands and its camps. These hills once fed Alterac's mountain fortresses, but now shelter the band's strongest base.

sections.title: Breadbasket to Bandit Stronghold
sections.body: Before the Second War broke Alterac apart, grain and livestock from the Uplands fed its mountain fortresses. When the kingdom fell into ruin, honest folk left their farms behind. Dispossessed nobles and cutthroats formed the Syndicate, set on taking back what they believed was stolen from them by force. Its camps, patrols, and outposts now fill the hills. Dandred's Fold lies along the western borders.

sections.title: A Seat of Shadows
sections.body: The Syndicate keeps its strongest forces in the Uplands. There, high-ranking conspirators oversee its operations, including Baron Vardus, who is aligned with the shadowy leaders guiding Alterac's remaining nobility. From these hills they direct brigands, raid neighboring valleys, and resist both the Alliance and Horde. Travelers on the northeastern ridges meet entrenched highwaymen who claim the range as their sovereign soil.

faq.q: What was the Uplands originally used for?
faq.answer: The Uplands once fed Alterac's mountain fortresses with grain and livestock. It was the kingdom's main agricultural region before war and betrayal brought its downfall.
The Syndicate controls the Uplands. Alterac's former nobles and their bandit network have built several camps here, where their forces are strongest.
The Uplands lies in the northeastern highlands of the Alterac Mountains. Dandred's Fold sits along its western edge.
Baron Vardus is an influential Syndicate noble who oversees operations in the Uplands. He directs bandits and conspirators seeking to reclaim Alterac.

angles.text: As a rogue, you can see how displaced nobles organized the Syndicate's bandit network into a lethal force.
As a human, you see Alterac's fall in these hills. Once they fed a flourishing kingdom; now cutthroats and ruined ambitions hold them.
